name: Textual
tagline: Python TUI framework with DOM, CSS, widgets and web serving

license.notes: Toad (Will McGugan's agent front end on Textual) is AGPL-3.0.

backing: Created by Will McGugan; Textualize Ltd (VC-backed) wound down in mid-2025 and Textual continues as an open-source project maintained mainly by McGugan (now on sabbatical, building Toad).

adoption.downloads: 14.5M/week, 55.5M/month on PyPI (pypistats.org recent); much of it transitive
notable_users: Posting (HTTP client, shown in textual-serve docs)
Many Python devtools and agent front ends (e.g. gentui AG-UI client)
adoption.summary: The dominant Python TUI framework, with very high PyPI volume and a large app ecosystem.

maintainability.recent_activity: 1 commit and 1 merged PR since 2026-07-11 (GitHub API): effectively dormant for 3 months
maintainability.bus_factor: low: willmcgugan has ~7,000 of the commits; the company that employed the other core devs closed in 2025
maintainability.summary: Mature and stable ('mature and battle-tested' per McGugan) but now a one-person project with activity dropping off.

architecture.summary: Retained mode: an App owns a DOM of Widget objects composed in Python (compose() yields children), styled by Textual CSS (TCSS) with selectors, layout (grid/horizontal/vertical/dock) and live reload. Reactive attributes trigger refresh; message passing between widgets is async (asyncio). A compositor (inherited from Rich's Segment model) merges overlapping widgets into a final segment list and only updates changed regions. Output drivers target terminals and, via textual-serve/textual-web, a browser.
key_points: DOM + CSS selectors (query_one('#id'), query('.cls')) addressable at runtime
Compositor over Rich Segments; partial screen updates
Pilot (App.run_test) drives an app headlessly: press keys, click selectors, pause, screenshot to SVG
textual run --dev: live CSS editing + devtools console (logs, events)
textual serve: any app in a browser with a few lines

claims.text: Compositor design for partial updates and overlapping widgets, described as 'algorithms for high performance terminal apps'
Dev mode: CSS changes 'reflected in the terminal a few milliseconds later'

performance.summary: Design write-ups but no published frames/sec or update-throughput benchmarks found.

agent_usability.how: Code generation, plus in-process automation via Pilot (run_test). Third-party MCP servers wrap Pilot (discohead/textual-mcp-server, 4 stars: 'drive Textual TUI apps headlessly'). Toad is the inverse: a Textual UI for agents over the Agent Client Protocol, not agents driving Textual.
agent_usability.integration_effort: Moderate: write or adopt an MCP wrapper around Pilot; the agent then gets selector-addressed clicks/keys and SVG screenshots of a headless instance (not the user's live one).
agent_usability.readback: Good in-process: the DOM can be queried by CSS selector, widget state read, and App.save_screenshot()/Pilot produce SVG renders. No built-in external socket for a live app.
agent_usability.granular_edits: In-process code can mutate any widget by id/selector and change styles; from outside only via a custom wrapper.
agent_usability.summary: The most introspectable of the mainstream frameworks (DOM + selectors + screenshots), but agent access is in-process/test-harness, not a live-instance protocol.

score_notes.ui_as_data: compose() in Python plus TCSS; CSS is data, widget tree is code
score_notes.agent_drivable: Pilot is an API but only for a test/headless instance; MCP wrappers are third-party and tiny
score_notes.granular_edits: Selector-addressed mutation exists in-process, not as a protocol
score_notes.teaching: textual serve, SVG screenshots and live CSS make demos easy; no tour features
score_notes.maturity: Widely used; dev slowdown after Textualize closed keeps it off 5

steelman: Textual is the closest thing the terminal has to a browser: a real DOM you can query by CSS selector, a real stylesheet language with live reload, a compositor that does overlapping layers and partial updates, a rich widget set (DataTable, TextArea with tree-sitter, Markdown, Tree, Tabs), and an app that runs unchanged in a web browser via textual serve. Its Pilot test driver already gives you what agents need in principle — press keys, click a selector, wait for idle, take an SVG screenshot — and the DOM means an agent can address 'the button with id save' instead of cell coordinates. It is MIT, battle-tested by thousands of apps and millions of weekly installs, and its author has gone all-in on agents with Toad. For Python shops it is the obvious substrate, and a thin MCP over Pilot gets you most of an agent-drivable TUI.
weaknesses: Textualize the company closed in 2025; main branch has had one commit since 2026-07-11
UI is Python code, not a value: you cannot push or diff a whole UI
No live-instance control protocol; MCP wrappers are third-party and immature
Python/asyncio startup and per-frame overhead; no published throughput numbers

relation_to_scene.overlap: Addressable widget tree (ids/selectors), stylesheet-driven theming, headless driving with keys/clicks and rendered screenshots, web serving.
relation_to_scene.scene_reinvents: Selector-addressed nodes, a layout/style system, screenshot readback and a headless test driver — Textual has had these, polished, for years.
borrow: Pilot's verbs (press, click(selector, offset), hover, pause/wait-for-idle) as the shape of scene's key/mouse ops
CSS-selector addressing in addition to plain ids for patch/click
SVG screenshot export of the cell frame for docs and readback
textual serve's idea: the same scene served to a browser
relation_to_scene.gap_left: A UI that is one serializable JSON value pushed/patched over a socket into a live (not test) instance, data streams bypassing the model at thousands/s, hot-swap upgrade, kitty pixel layer beneath text, agent time travel.
relation_to_scene.verdict_why: Textual's addressing, driver verbs and screenshot readback are proven designs scene should copy, but its code-defined UI and Python runtime don't fit a Rust JSON-scene.
